activityGoals.name: Increment/Decrement Operators (Case 1)
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that performs increment/decrement operations on variable a (with initial value of 4) and variable b (with initial value of 5) and prints the following output as the result of these operations:\n-1\n3

commentList: We define variable a and set its initial value to 4.
We define variable b and set its initial value to 5.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Perform the operations and print the first output

commentList: The expression in this println statement produces the first output. The subtraction operator uses original value of variables a (i.e., 4) and b (i.e., 5), thus generating the result of -1.

a++ evaluates to 4 and then increments variable a by 1. Therefore, the value on the left-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 4.
b-- evaluates to 5 and then decrements variable b by 1. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 5.
Note that when we have post-increment/post-decrement operator, the variable gets incremented/decremented by 1, but the original value of that variable will be used in the statement.

lineList.content: //Step 3: Perform the operations and print the second output

commentList: The expression in this println statement produces the second output. The subtraction operator uses value of variables a and b after the pre-increment and pre-decrement operations are performed.

++a evaluates to 6 because, when program reaches here, variable a holds 5 and it gets incremented by 1 before the left-hand side of the subtraction operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the left-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 6.
--b evaluates to 3 because, when program reaches here, variable b holds 4 and it gets decremented by 1 before the right-hand side of the subtraction operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the subtraction operator will be 3.
Note that when we have pre-increment/pre-decrement operator, the variable gets incremented/decremented by 1, and the updated value of that variable will be used in the statement.

activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that performs increment/decrement operations on variable a (with initial value of 8) and variable b (with initial value of 3) and prints the following output as the result of these operations:\n10\n12

commentList: We define variable a and set its initial value to 8.
We define variable b and set its initial value to 3.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Perform the operations and print the first output

commentList: The expression in this println statement produces the first output. The addition operator uses original value of variable a (i.e., 8) but decremented value of variable b (i.e., 2), thus generating the result of 10.

a++ evaluates to 8 and then increments variable a by 1. Therefore, the value on the left-hand side of the addition operator will be 8.
--b evaluates to 2 because variable b holds 3 and it gets decremented by 1 before the right-hand side of the addition operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the addition operator will be 2.

Note that when we have post-increment operator, the variable gets incremented by 1, but the original value of that variable will be used in the statement.
Also note that when we have pre-decrement operator, the variable gets decremented by 1 and the updated value of that variable will be used in the statement.

activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that performs increment/decrement operations on variable a (with initial value of 6) and variable b (with initial value of 1) and prints the following output as the result of these operations:\n5\n7

commentList: We define variable a and set its initial value to 6.
We define variable b and set its initial value to 1.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Perform the operations and print the first output

commentList: The expression in this println statement produces the first output. The addition operator uses the decremented value of variable b (i.e., 0), thus generating the result of 5.

--b evaluates to 0 because variable b holds 1 and it gets decremented by 1 before the right-hand side of the addition operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the addition operator will be 0.
